findings.plain_summary: OPM is seeking public comment through December 18, 2026 on a new information collection, Form RI 20-129 (Annuitant Verification Form), which would verify the identity of annuitants who ask to change their contact information. The notice estimates 750 respondents at 15 minutes each (188 total burden hours) and says the verification will decide whether a requester gets access to the annuitant's account, but the summary mentions only that comments are invited.

items.headline: Form RI 20-129 is created to verify identity before contact information changes
items.what_changes: OPM is creating a new form that annuitants must complete when they ask to change contact information, to confirm the requester's identity before any change is made.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM has created Form RI 20-129 to verify the identity of an annuitant who has requested changes to contact information.

items.headline: Verification decides whether a requester gets access to the annuitant's account
items.what_changes: The result of the identity verification controls whether the person making the request is given access to the annuitant's account.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The verification will determine whether the individual is provided access to the annuitant's account.

items.headline: Stated reason: current contact-change channels cannot reliably verify identity
items.what_changes: OPM says contact-change requests arrive through channels that do not allow adequate identity checks, such as a caller who cannot answer identification questions correctly, and the form is the response to that gap.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM receives requests to change contact information by various means of communication that do not provide sufficient opportunity to OPM to verify the identity of the individual initiating the request, such as when a caller is unable to provide a correct response to identification questions.

items.headline: Burden estimate: 750 respondents, 188 total hours
items.what_changes: The collection is estimated to involve 750 individuals or households at 15 minutes each, for 188 total burden hours, with use on an occasional basis.
items.speaker: OPM

items.headline: Comment period closes December 18, 2026
items.what_changes: Public comments on the new collection are accepted until December 18, 2026, and OPM encourages them.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Comments are encouraged and will be accepted until December 18, 2026.

could_not_determine: The questions asked on Form RI 20-129 and what identifying information annuitants must supply
Whether completing the form is mandatory for contact-information changes or optional, and what happens to requests that are not verified
Whether verification is required for every contact-information change or only for certain channels
How many contact-information change requests OPM currently receives and how many it expects to route through the form
The basis for the 750-respondent and 15-minute estimates
Privacy handling, retention, and system-of-records coverage for information collected on the form
Whether OPM has submitted the collection to OMB and when approval is expected
Any comments received, since this is a 60-day notice still in its comment period
